mainTopic: The soldiers' atonement for gazing; the משנה on hair and ornaments a woman may wear on שבת; רב on the courtyard and on מראית העין
overview: The amud opens by finishing a lesson about the soldiers who fought מדין: they needed a כפרה because they gazed at forbidden sights. רב ששת adds that gazing at even a woman's little finger for pleasure is as serious as gazing at her private area. A new משנה then lists what a woman may wear outside on שבת: hair strands, sewn head ornaments, a מוך, and items in her mouth. A כבול and a פאה נכרית are allowed only in the חצר, and רבי and the חכמים disagree about a false tooth. The גמרא explains why all three sources of hair had to be listed, and a ברייתא forbids a mismatch between a young girl's hair and an old woman's hair. רב rules that whatever is forbidden in the street is also forbidden in the חצר, except the כבול and the פאה נכרית. עולא explains this exception: the חכמים did not want her to become unattractive to her husband, a concern רבי עקיבא also shows. Finally, רב rules that what is forbidden because of מראית העין is forbidden even in private. A plugged bell is used to challenge this, and the גמרא answers that it is a dispute between תנאים, with the proof coming on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the soldiers needed atonement
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of an earlier answer: the soldiers of the war with מדין needed a כפרה because they 'fed their eyes' on forbidden sights.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...because they fed their eyes from immodesty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began earlier. Earlier it asked why the soldiers who fought מדין needed a כפרה, and here it answers: because they looked at forbidden sights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The soldiers did not commit any forbidden act, and none of them were lost in battle. Still, they brought ornaments as an offering to atone. The גמרא explains that their sin was in what they let their eyes look at, not in any physical action.

keyTerms.meaning: They 'fed' or nourished their eyes, meaning they gazed for pleasure
Nakedness; something forbidden and immodest to look at
Atonement

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new topic. It is the last part of a sentence that began on the previous section of the דף.

phrases.english: because they fed their eyes
from nakedness (forbidden sights).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the question asked on the previous amud: why the soldiers needed a כפרה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They needed atonement because they gazed at forbidden sights
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the soldiers of the war with מדין needed a כפרה

steps.title: רב ששת: outer and inner ornaments are listed together
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains why the פסוק lists outer jewelry, such as a bracelet, together with intimate jewelry, the כומז. It teaches that gazing at even a woman's little finger is like gazing at her private area.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Why did the verse list the outer ornaments together with the inner ornaments? To teach you that anyone who gazes at the little finger of a woman is considered as if he gazed at her private area.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת asks a question about how the פסוק is worded, and then he answers it himself. The answer explains even more why the soldiers needed atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists ornaments worn on the outside, like a bracelet, next to the כומז, which was worn on an intimate place. רב ששת says the two are placed side by side to teach that looking for pleasure is serious even when the body part is normally visible. So the soldiers needed a כפרה even for gazing at the visible jewelry.

keyTerms.meaning: Outer ornaments, worn on visible places such as the arm
Inner ornaments, worn on intimate places (the כּוּמָז)
One who gazes intently
The private area, the place of nakedness

steps.whatToRemember: The soldiers' atonement was for improper looking. רב ששת teaches that even gazing at a visible part of a woman, done for pleasure, is treated seriously.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line is a classic source for the seriousness of improper gazing.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
For what reason did the verse list
outer ornaments
together with inner ornaments?
To tell you:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמִּסְתַּכֵּל בְּאֶצְבַּע קְטַנָּה שֶׁל אִשָּׁה
phrases.english: anyone who gazes at the little finger of a woman
is as if he gazed at her private area.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מִפְּנֵי מָה מָנָה הַכָּתוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and explains the claim that the soldiers' sin was in their looking
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gazing at even a small visible part of a woman for pleasure is as serious as gazing at her private area

steps.title: משנה: a woman may go out with hair strands
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. A woman may go out on שבת with strands of hair woven into her hair, whether they come from her own hair, another woman's, or an animal's.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman may go out with strands of hair, whether from her own, from her friend's, or from an animal's.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here, continuing the topic of what a woman may wear outside on שבת. It permits hair strands from any of three sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hair strands are woven into her hair and become part of her hairstyle. So there is no worry that she will take them off and carry them in a public area, and they do not count as carrying. The משנה adds that the source of the hair makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; this marks that a new משנה is beginning
May go out (into a public area on שבת)
Strands of hair woven into her braids
Her friend; another woman

phrases.english: MISHNA: A woman may go out
with strands of hair,
whether from her own,
whether from her friend's,
whether from an animal's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: back to the הלכות of going out on שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hair strands are permitted on שבת regardless of where the hair came from

steps.title: משנה: forehead band and hanging ornaments when sewn
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. A woman may also go out with a טוטפת, a band across the forehead, and with סרביטין, ornaments hanging toward the cheeks, as long as they are sewn on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she may go out with a טוטפת and with סרביטין, when they are sewn.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds two more head ornaments that are permitted on שבת, with one condition: they must be sewn on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ornaments that are loose might fall off, or she might take them off to show someone, and then carry them four אמות in a public area. Sewing them on removes that worry, so they are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A decorative band worn across the forehead
Ornaments hanging down toward the cheeks
Sewn on, so they will not come off

steps.confusionAlert: It is not obvious from the words alone whether 'when they are sewn' refers only to the סרביטין or also to the טוטפת. Do not assume either way; the commentaries discuss this.
steps.whatToRemember: Items that are firmly attached, like woven hair or sewn ornaments, are permitted because there is no worry she will remove them and carry.

phrases.english: And with a forehead band (totefet),
and with hanging ornaments (sarvitin)
when they are sewn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of items permitted in the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טוטפת and סרביטין are permitted on שבת when they are sewn on

steps.title: Woolen cap and wig only to the courtyard, and cotton pads are allowed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows a כבול and a פאה נכרית only in a חצר. It also allows a מוך in the ear, in the sandal, or one prepared for נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: She may go out with a woolen cap or a wig, but only into the courtyard. She may also go out with a cotton pad in her ear, a cotton pad in her sandal, or a cotton pad she prepared for her menstrual flow.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing what a woman may wear outside on שבת. Here it adds a limit for some items and a permission for others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כבול and the פאה נכרית are allowed in the חצר but not in רשות הרבים. The worry is that she might take them off in public and carry them. The three kinds of מוך are allowed because each one serves her body, so it counts as something she wears, not something she carries.

keyTerms.meaning: A woolen cap or hairnet
A wig, literally 'foreign hair'
A courtyard, a shared private area and not the public domain
A wad of cotton or soft cloth
A woman during her menstrual period

steps.confusionAlert: 'לחצר' means ONLY to the courtyard. The cap and wig are not allowed in רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: With a woolen cap and with a wig, to the courtyard.
phrases.notes: Only into the courtyard, not into the public domain.

phrases.english: With a cotton pad that is in her ear,
and with a cotton pad that is in her sandal,
and with a cotton pad that she prepared for her menstruation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of permitted items from Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כבול and a פאה נכרית are permitted only in a חצר. A מוך in the ear, in the sandal, or for נדה is permitted.

steps.title: Pepper, salt, or anything in her mouth, if put in before שבת
steps.stepSummary: A woman may go out with pepper, salt, or anything held in her mouth. She may not put it in for the first time on שבת, and if it falls out she may not put it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: She may go out with a peppercorn, a grain of salt, or anything placed in her mouth. But she may not put it in for the first time on שבת, and if it falls out, she may not put it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה allows things kept in the mouth, such as items for healing or for bad breath. It then adds two limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The item may stay in her mouth only if she put it there before שבת. If it falls out, putting it back on שבת is the same as putting it in for the first time, so that is not allowed either.

keyTerms.meaning: A peppercorn
A grain or lump of salt
At the outset, for the first time
She may not put it back

phrases.english: With a peppercorn, and with a grain of salt,
and with anything that is placed inside her mouth,
phrases.notes: For example, for healing or against bad breath.

phrases.english: as long as she does not put it in for the first time on Shabbat,
and if it fell out, she may not put it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another category to the משנה's list: items kept in the mouth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items in the mouth are permitted if put in before שבת. They may not be put in for the first time on שבת or put back after falling out.

steps.title: Dispute over a false tooth or a gold tooth
steps.stepSummary: רבי permits going out with a false tooth or a gold tooth. The חכמים forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A false tooth or a gold tooth: רבי permits going out with it, and the חכמים forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends its list with a מחלוקת about artificial teeth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים worry that she might take the tooth out, for example out of embarrassment, and then carry it in public. רבי does not share that worry, so for him the tooth counts as part of what she wears.

keyTerms.meaning: A false tooth, a tooth that has been inserted
רבי יהודה הנשיא, who compiled the משנה
Permits / forbid

phrases.english: A false tooth, a tooth of gold:
Rabbi permits, and the Sages forbid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה with a dispute instead of a simple ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי permits a false or gold tooth. The חכמים forbid it.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three kinds of rules. Some items are fully permitted (hair strands, sewn ornaments, מוך). Some are permitted only in the חצר (כבול, פאה נכרית). Some are permitted only with conditions (items in the mouth). It ends with a מחלוקת about teeth.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed to list both her own hair and another woman's hair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with צריכא, explaining why each kind of hair in the משנה had to be listed. If the משנה had mentioned only her own hair, we might have forbidden another woman's hair because it is unattractive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is necessary to list each case. If the משנה had taught us only about her own hair, we would say it is allowed because it is not unattractive. But another woman's hair, which is unattractive, we would say is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first case in the משנה, the hair strands from Step 3, and explains why all three sources of hair are listed. This step is only the first half of the צריכא. It sets up the next move, where the גמרא will explain why the other case is also needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her own hair matches her, so there is no reason she would take it off. Another woman's hair may look different and embarrass her. She might then remove it and carry it in public, so without the משנה's explicit ruling we might have forbidden it. The משנה lists another woman's hair to tell us it is allowed anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
'And it is necessary': a formula explaining why each case had to be listed
It taught us
Repulsive, unattractive
I would say no (it is not permitted)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אימא לא' is NOT the final הלכה. It is the mistaken assumption (הוה אמינא) we would have made. The משנה lists another woman's hair precisely to show that it IS permitted.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And it is necessary,
phrases.notes: Each case in the משנה is needed.

phrases.english: for if it had taught us only her own hair,
we would say that is because it is not repulsive,
phrases.notes: So she has no reason to remove it.

phrases.english: but her friend's hair, which is repulsive,
I would say no.
phrases.notes: The mistaken assumption that the משנה comes to correct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the משנה to the גמרא, going back to the hair-strands clause in Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Listing another woman's hair is necessary, because otherwise we might have forbidden it as unattractive and likely to be removed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: when the משנה lists several similar cases, the גמרא explains why each one teaches something new.

steps.title: Why animal hair also had to be mentioned
steps.stepSummary: Even if we knew another woman's hair is allowed, we would still think animal hair is forbidden, so all three cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught us only about another woman's hair, we would say: that is allowed because it comes from her own kind, a human. But animal hair is not from her own kind, so we would say it is not allowed. That is why the משנה needed to teach all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא it started in the last step. It shows that animal hair needed its own mention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed that her own hair alone would not teach us about another woman's hair. Now the גמרא shows that another woman's hair alone would not teach us about animal hair. Animal hair is not human, so we might fear she would find it unpleasant, take it off, and carry it in the street. Each case adds something new.

keyTerms.meaning: It taught us
Of her own kind (human hair)
That of an animal
I would say no (it is not allowed)

steps.whatToRemember: All three kinds of hair are allowed. Each one had to be listed because we could not learn one from another.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only about her friend's hair —
that is allowed because it is of her own kind,
phrases.notes: Human hair is not unpleasant to her, so she will not take it off.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דִּבְהֵמָה לָאו בַּר מִינַהּ הוּא
phrases.english: but animal hair is not of her own kind,
so I would say it is not allowed. Therefore it is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the צריכא begun in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה needed to list her own hair, another woman's hair, and animal hair separately.

steps.title: A girl and an old woman may not swap hair
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds a limit: a ילדה may not wear a זקנה's hair, and a זקנה may not wear a ילדה's hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: This is allowed only as long as a young girl does not go out wearing an old woman's hair, and an old woman does not go out wearing a young girl's hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that limits the permission to wear another woman's hair. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed hair from another woman, but the ברייתא says it must not be a mismatch in age. When the hair does not fit the woman, there is a worry she may take it off and carry it in the street. The ברייתא names two mismatches.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (introduces a ברייתא)
As long as / provided that
A young girl
An old woman

phrases.english: It was taught: provided that
a young girl does not go out with an old woman's hair
and an old woman does not go out with a young girl's hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the permission for another woman's hair discussed in steps 8-9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrowed hair is allowed only if a girl does not wear an old woman's hair and an old woman does not wear a girl's hair.

steps.title: Why would a girl ever wear an old woman's hair?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the case of an old woman wearing young hair, but asks why the ברייתא would mention a girl wearing old hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense to mention an old woman wearing a young girl's hair, because that makes her look better. But why mention a young girl wearing an old woman's hair? That makes her look worse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second case in the ברייתא. It says this case is unrealistic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An old woman would want young-looking hair, so that case could really happen. A young girl would never want to look old, so she would never wear such hair in the first place. Why would the ברייתא bother to forbid something nobody does?

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable that... (sets up a contrast)
Praise / something flattering
Why?
Disgrace / something unflattering

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking why the girl's case is forbidden. It is asking why the ברייתא mentions it at all, since no girl would do it.

phrases.english: It is understandable regarding an old woman with a girl's hair —
it is flattering for her.
But a girl with an old woman's hair, why?
It is a disgrace for her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of the ברייתא quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's case of a ילדה wearing a זקנה's hair
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No girl would wear hair that makes her look old, so there is no reason to forbid it.

steps.title: The second case was taught only to match the first
steps.stepSummary: Because the ברייתא taught the old woman's case, it also taught the girl's case to keep the wording parallel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the ברייתא taught the case of an old woman with a girl's hair, it also taught the case of a girl with an old woman's hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the girl's case is not a real worry. It was added only to balance the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real teaching is the old woman's case. The girl's case was added for style, as a matching pair. This is the familiar אַיְּידִי answer: one case is mentioned only because of the case next to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because (it taught one case, it taught the other)
Also

steps.whyThisMatters: The אַיְּידִי answer comes up all over ש״ס. It tells us that not every case in a teaching is a real practical concern. Some cases appear only for parallel wording.

phrases.english: Since it taught an old woman with a girl's hair,
it also taught a girl with an old woman's hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The girl's case is a real practical concern.
steps.terutzMaskana: The girl's case is mentioned only to match the old woman's case.

steps.title: רב: only the cap and the wig are allowed in the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a כבול and a פאה נכרית in the חצר. רב says anything forbidden in the street is also forbidden in the courtyard, except these two.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a woman may go out with a woolen cap or a wig into the courtyard. רב said: Anything the חכמים forbade wearing into the public domain is also forbidden to wear into a courtyard, except a woolen cap and a wig.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. רב gives a general rule and names these two items as the only exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if an item may not be worn into רשות הרבים, the חכמים forbid it even in a חצר. The worry is that she might forget and walk out into the street. The כבול and the פאה נכרית are special exceptions to this rule, and the גמרא will explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: A woolen cap or hair covering
A wig
A courtyard
The public domain
Except for

steps.whyThisMatters: רב turns the משנה's detail into a general rule with a short list of exceptions. This sets up the next discussion about why these two items get special treatment.

phrases.english: With a woolen cap and with a wig to the courtyard.
Rav said: Anything that the Sages forbade
to go out with into the public domain,
it is forbidden to go out with into the courtyard —
phrases.notes: Lest she forget and go out to the street.

phrases.english: except for a woolen cap and a wig.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכָבוּל וּבְפֵאָה נׇכְרִית לֶחָצֵר. אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה (step 5) and opens a new topic about the courtyard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything forbidden in רשות הרבים is also forbidden in a חצר, except a כבול and a פאה נכרית.

steps.title: רבי ענני בר ששון says every ornament is like a woolen cap
steps.stepSummary: רבי ענני בר ששון, quoting רבי ישמעאל, says that all ornaments have the same status as a כבול and may be worn in the חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ענני בר ששון said in the name of רבי ישמעאל: Everything is like a woolen cap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion that argues with רב. רב permitted only two items in the חצר, while רבי ענני בר ששון permits every ornament there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that anything forbidden in the street is also forbidden in the חצר, except a כבול and a פאה נכרית. רבי ענני בר ששון makes the כבול the model for everything. In his view, all ornaments are permitted in the חצר, just like the כבול.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disagrees with רב here
In the name of
Everything is like a woolen cap, so all ornaments are permitted in the courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ענני is not saying that everything may be worn in the street. He is only saying that everything may be worn in the חצר, the way a כבול may be.

phrases.english: Rabbi Anani bar Sason
said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
Everything is like a woolen cap.
phrases.notes: Every ornament may be worn into the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲנָנִי בַּר שָׂשׂוֹן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opinion that argues with רב's rule from Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All ornaments have the status of a כבול and are permitted in the חצר.

steps.title: The משנה lists only two items, which fits רב but not רבי ענני
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions only a כבול and a פאה נכרית for the חצר. That fits רב, but it is a problem for רבי ענני בר ששון.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: With a woolen cap and with a wig, into the courtyard. Granted, according to רב it works well. But according to רבי ענני בר ששון, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ענני בר ששון using the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every ornament were permitted in the חצר, the משנה would not need to name just two items. The fact that it names only two suggests that only those two are permitted, which is exactly what רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה
A wig made of someone else's hair
Granted, this works for one opinion
It is difficult

phrases.english: We learned: With a woolen cap and with a wig, into the courtyard.
Granted, according to Rav, it works well,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי עֲנָנִי בַּר שָׂשׂוֹן קַשְׁיָא!
phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Anani bar Sason, it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב נִיחָא אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי עֲנָנִי בַּר שָׂשׂוֹן קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the opinion stated in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ענני בר ששון's claim that all ornaments are permitted in the חצר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists only two items, which implies that other ornaments are forbidden in the חצר.

steps.title: רבי ענני follows a תנא who may argue with the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ענני was quoting רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי, who is a תנא and is allowed to disagree with the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In whose name did רבי ענני בר ששון say this? In the name of רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי. רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי is a תנא, and he disagrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי ענני by showing that his source is a תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא normally cannot argue with a משנה. A תנא, however, has the authority to disagree with it. Since רבי ענני is passing on the view of רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי, a תנא, the משנה is not a problem for him. His view is simply a different תנאי opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: In whose name?
He is a תנא, so he may disagree
The תנא whose view רבי ענני quotes

phrases.english: Rabbi Anani bar Sason,
in whose name does he say it?
In the name of Rabbi Yishmael bar Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר יוֹסֵי תַּנָּא הוּא וּפְלִיג.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yishmael bar Yosei is a Tanna, and he disagrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the source as a תנא who may argue with the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רבי ענני's view had to fit our משנה, so the משנה's short list of two items contradicted it.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is passing on the view of a תנא who disagrees with the משנה.

steps.title: According to רב, why are these two items different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב permits only the כבול and the פאה נכרית in the חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב, what is different about these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב and asks for the reason behind his two exceptions. This sets up עולא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's general rule is that whatever is forbidden in the street is also forbidden in the חצר. The גמרא wants to know what makes these two items deserve an exception to that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
These

phrases.english: And Rav, what is different about these?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב's view from Step 13 after dealing with רבי ענני.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the כבול and the פאה נכרית are allowed in the חצר according to רב.

steps.title: עולא: so she does not become unattractive to her husband
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that these items were permitted so that a woman would not become unattractive to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: So that she will not become unattractive to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question about רב's two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a woman could not wear any ornament even at home in the חצר, she might look unattractive to her husband. To prevent that, the חכמים permitted these two items in the חצר.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the reason
Become unattractive or disliked
Her husband

phrases.english: Ulla said:
So that she will not become unattractive to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תִּתְגַּנֶּה עַל בַּעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exception exists so that a woman will not become unattractive to her husband.

steps.title: Support from רבי עקיבא's teaching about a menstruating woman
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the same concern. The early elders forbade a נדה to adorn herself, but רבי עקיבא rejected that because it would make her unattractive to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And she who is unwell in her menstruation.' The early elders said she may not paint her eyes, may not rouge her face, and may not adorn herself with colored clothes. Then רבי עקיבא came and taught: If so, you make her unattractive to her husband, and her husband will end up divorcing her. Rather, what does the verse teach with 'And she who is unwell in her menstruation'? She remains in her menstrual status until she enters the water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support עולא's reason. It shows that the חכמים were careful not to make a woman unattractive to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The early elders read the פסוק as a reason to forbid a נדה from making herself attractive. רבי עקיבא rejected this because it could lead to divorce. He read the פסוק differently: she stays a נדה until she goes to the מקוה. This is the same concern עולא used to explain why the כבול and the פאה נכרית are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: And she who is unwell in her menstruation (ויקרא 15:33)
The early elders
Paint her eyes
Put rouge on her face
Until she immerses in a מקוה

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, the כבול and the פאה נכרית are permitted in the חצר because the חכמים did not want a woman to become unattractive to her husband. רבי עקיבא shows the same concern.

phrases.english: As it was taught: "And she who is unwell in her menstruation":
The early elders said
that she may not paint her eyes and may not rouge her face,
and may not adorn herself with colored clothes,
until Rabbi Akiva came and taught:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן — אַתָּה מְגַנָּהּ עַל בַּעְלָהּ,
phrases.english: If so, you make her unattractive to her husband,
and her husband will end up divorcing her.
Rather, what does the verse teach with "And she who is unwell in her menstruation"?
She remains in her menstrual status until she enters the water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports עולא's reason from Step 18.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's reason, that the חכמים avoided making a woman unattractive to her husband
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבי עקיבא's rejection of the early elders' restrictions on a נדה

steps.title: רב: what is forbidden for appearances is forbidden even in private
steps.stepSummary: רב says that anything the חכמים forbade because of מראית העין is forbidden even in the most private rooms.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that רב said: Wherever the חכמים forbade something because of how it looks, it is forbidden even in the innermost rooms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a general rule from רב. It matches his approach that what is forbidden in the street is also forbidden in the חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something forbidden because of how it looks might seem fine where nobody can see. רב says no: the חכמים did not divide up their rules by place, so it stays forbidden everywhere. This fits his view that ornaments forbidden in the street are also forbidden in the חצר.

keyTerms.meaning: How something looks to others; something that appears forbidden
The innermost, most private rooms
The student who reports רב's teaching

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule about rabbinic decrees: a decree based on appearances usually applies even in private.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, anything forbidden because of מראית העין is forbidden even when nobody can see.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Wherever the Sages forbade something
because of how it looks,
it is forbidden even in the innermost rooms.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאָסְרוּ חֲכָמִים מִפְּנֵי מַרְאִית הָעַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a general rule from רב that matches his strict view about the חצר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything forbidden because of מראית העין is forbidden even in completely private places.

steps.title: A plugged bell is forbidden outside but allowed in the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's rule. A plugged bell on an animal is forbidden because of how it looks, yet a ברייתא permits it inside the חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: An animal may not go out with a bell, even if the bell is plugged. And another ברייתא taught: A person may plug a bell on the animal's neck and walk with it in the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two sources that seem to contradict רב. Together they show a מראית העין rule that does not apply in a private courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plugged bell makes no sound, so it is forbidden only because it looks like the owner is taking the animal to market. That is a מראית העין concern. Since the ברייתא permits it in the חצר, it seems that a מראית העין rule can be relaxed in private, which goes against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה
A bell hung on an animal's neck
Plugged, so the bell cannot ring
Another ברייתא taught
A private courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is about an animal wearing a bell, not about a woman's jewelry. The גמרא uses it because it follows the same pattern: something forbidden only because of how it looks.

phrases.english: We learned: And not with a bell
phrases.notes: The משנה about what an animal may go out with on שבת.

phrases.english: even though it is plugged.
phrases.notes: It makes no sound, so the problem is only how it looks.

phrases.english: And another baraita taught:
He may plug a bell on its neck
and walk with it in the courtyard.
phrases.notes: This permits it in private, which seems to contradict רב.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: וְלֹא בְּזוֹג אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁפָּקוּק. וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's rule from Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that anything forbidden because of מראית העין is forbidden even in the most private rooms.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plugged bell is forbidden only because of מראית העין, yet a ברייתא permits it in the חצר. So a מראית העין rule can be relaxed in private.

steps.title: This is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the question of the bell in the courtyard is a dispute between תנאים. It begins to quote a ברייתא that shows this.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as it was taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying different תנאים disagree about this. It is setting up the next move, a ברייתא that will show the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not have to agree with every ברייתא. The ברייתא that permits the bell in the courtyard follows one opinion, and רב follows the other opinion, which forbids it even in private.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim, as it was taught:
phrases.notes: This introduces the ברייתא, which is quoted on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between תנאים: רב follows the other opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא permitting the plugged bell in the courtyard disproves רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: That ברייתא follows only one opinion. Another תנא forbids it even in private, and רב agrees with him.
